h1: The 7 Best Push-Button Start Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Push-Button Start Mowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven push-button start lawn mowers, from full-size self-propelled EGO and Greenworks to small cordless 16-inch decks.
summary: The EGO Power+ LM2134SP-2 is our best overall, pairing a push-button key start with self-propelled drive on a 21 inch deck. The Greenworks 80V self-propelled is the cheaper way to the same feature set, and the EGO LM2114 is the push-drive alternative. For small lawns, the Greenworks 40V 16-Inch is the dependable compact pick.
intro: A push-button start sounds like a small convenience until you compare it with a gas pull cord on a cold morning. The trap is that battery mowers vary wildly in what comes in the box. Some sell a bare tool, some include a spare battery, and the voltage number alone tells you little.

We reviewed seven push-button mowers on paper, ranking them on deck width, drive type, battery and charger included, and price tier. The ranking leans on listings and owner reports, with no lab claims.

products.name: EGO Power+ 21-Inch Cordless Electric Self-Propelled Lawn Mower (LM2134SP-2)
products.verdict: Push-button key start and self-propelled drive on a full 21 inch deck.
products.description:
The EGO LM2134SP-2 has a 21-inch deck, self-propelled drive and a push-button key start on EGO's cordless battery platform.

It ranks first because it combines the two features this guide cares about, an easy start and a drive that pulls the mower along. Compared with the LM2114 below, it adds self-propel for the $500+ tier.

Buy it if you want a full-size mower with every convenience. The caveat is that it is the priciest pick here.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting push-button starting plus self-propel.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Lawn Mower, 4.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: Self-propelled with an 80V 4.0Ah pack for less than the EGO.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V has a 21-inch deck, self-propelled drive, a push-button key start and an 80V 4.0Ah battery plus charger in the box.

It ranks second because it matches the EGO LM2134SP-2 on features while dropping into the $200-500 bracket. The higher-voltage pack is a talking point, though the battery platform is a different brand ecosystem.

Choose it for self-propel without the top-tier price. The caveat is that you buy into the Greenworks battery line.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting self-propel at a lower price.

products.name: EGO POWER+ 21-Inch Cordless Electric Lawn Mower with Battery, Charger (LM2114)
products.verdict: A 21 inch push mower on the 56V platform, battery included.
products.description:
The EGO LM2114 has a 21-inch cutting deck, a 56V battery platform, a battery and charger in the box and a push drive.

It ranks third because it drops the self-propel of the two above, which means more effort on larger lawns. It stays in the $200-500 bracket like the Greenworks 80V.

Buy it for a standard-size lawn where you want a proven push-button battery mower. The caveat is that there is no drive assistance.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 21-Inch Push Lawn Mower, 5.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A 21 inch push deck with a 60V 5.0Ah pack included.
products.description:
The Greenworks 60V has a 21-inch deck, a 60V 5.0Ah battery with charger included, push drive and a push-button key start.

It ranks fourth because it offers a bigger 5.0Ah pack than the Greenworks 80V but no self-propel. It is the full-width option for buyers who do not want to pay for drive assistance. Cost-wise it belongs to the $200-500 group.

Choose it for a full-width push mower with a larger battery. The caveat is that the 60V platform differs from the 80V and 40V lines.
products.idealFor: Full-width push mowing without paying for self-propel.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Lawn Mower, 4.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A compact 16 inch push-button mower with battery included.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V has a 16-inch deck, a 40V 4.0Ah battery and charger included, push drive and a push-button key start.

It ranks fifth because the deck is five inches narrower than the 21-inch group, though it is easier to store. It sits in the $200-500 bracket, which is pricey next to the 16-inch budget options below.

Choose it for small lawns where a compact mower is the priority. The caveat is that you pay more than for the generic 16-inch models.

products.name: MZK 40V 16-Inch 2-in-1 Brushless Cordless Push Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A 16 inch brushless 2-in-1 with a push-button key start.
products.description:
The MZK has a 16-inch deck, a 40V battery platform, a brushless motor and a push-button key start, as a 2-in-1 push mower.

It ranks sixth because it is from a lesser-known brand and the listing does not say what battery is included. It costs less than the Greenworks 40V. Spending runs in the $100-200 range.

Choose it for a small lawn when money is tight. The caveat is that you should confirm what comes in the box.
products.skipIf: You want a major battery ecosystem.

products.name: KOMASTY 40V 16-Inch Cordless Battery Powered Lawn Mower, 2-in-1 Mulching
products.verdict: Two 4.0Ah batteries and two chargers at the lowest price.
products.description:
The KOMASTY has a 16-inch deck, a 40V battery platform and a push-button key start, and it includes two 4.0Ah batteries and two chargers. It is a 2-in-1 mulching design.

It ranks last because the brand is the least established here. The second battery is its best feature, and it sits in the $50-100 bracket.

Choose it if you want a spare battery on a tight budget. The caveat is the unproven brand.
products.idealFor: Tight budgets that want a spare battery.

whatMatters.detail: A push-button key start replaces the pull cord with a safety key and a button. It matters because there is no yanking. Look for 'push-button' in the title or bullets.
Self-propelled mowers drive their own wheels. They help on slopes and big lawns but add weight. Look for the 'self-propelled' label.
Volts set power platform and amp-hours set runtime. A 5.0Ah pack runs longer than a 4.0Ah one. Check both numbers and the charger.
A 21-inch deck covers more per pass than a 16-inch deck. A wider deck is heavier and harder to store. Match width to lawn size.
Some listings include a spare battery or second charger. That can change the effective price. Read the included items line.

faq.q: What is a push-button key start?
faq.a: You insert a safety key and press a button instead of pulling a cord. All seven picks list it.
They buy a bare tool without a battery. Check the included items before ordering.
On a large or sloped lawn, yes. On a small lawn the extra weight is not worth it.

faq.q: How do I set up a battery mower?
faq.a: Charge the battery, insert it, insert the key and press the button. Follow the manual's safety steps.
Clean the deck after use and store the battery indoors. Check the manual for blade guidance.
The MZK and KOMASTY are 2-in-1 designs, and the KOMASTY is listed as mulching. Check the others.

finalTake: The EGO LM2134SP-2 is the best push-button start mower for buyers who want self-propel and a full deck. The Greenworks 80V is the cheaper path to the same features, and the Greenworks 40V is the compact option. Check what comes in the box first.
